intro_html: Ethiopia's national dish: chicken thighs braised in a deep red berbere and slow-cooked onion sauce, finished with hard boiled eggs. Each bowl brings a serious 54 grams of protein at just 574 calories for about $2.48. The onions cook down into the sauce itself, so there is no flour, no cream, and no filler.
cost_closing_html: About $2.48 a bowl for doro wat. Ethiopian restaurants charge $16 to $20 for this dish with injera, and most towns only have one place that makes it at all. Your fridge is now that place.
shop_smart: Chicken thighs at $17.36 for 7 pounds are the anchor, and thighs are the right cut here anyway; breasts would dry out in a long braise.

Berbere is the one specialty jar, and it is worth it: the batch uses about $7 worth and one jar keeps seasoning batch after batch. Check international aisles or online before paying spice-boutique prices.
Eighteen eggs for $2.14 turn each bowl into a two-protein meal. Eggs remain the cheapest protein upgrade in the store.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks and toss with the lemon juice and a big pinch of salt. Let them sit while you cook the onions.

Finely chop the red onions and cook them dry in your big pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, 15 to 20 minutes until soft and deeply golden. This slow onion melt is the backbone of doro wat, so do not rush it.
Add the vegetable oil, garlic, and ginger and cook 2 minutes. Stir in the berbere and paprika and toast 1 to 2 minutes until brick red and fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the chicken broth. Simmer 10 minutes to marry the sauce.
Add the chicken and simmer gently, partially covered, 25 to 30 minutes until it reaches 165 F and the sauce has thickened. Stir in the butter at the end for gloss.
Meanwhile, hard boil the eggs: 11 minutes in boiling water, then an ice bath, then peel. Prick or slash each egg lightly and let them warm in the sauce for the last 5 minutes.
Portion into 14 containers with a hard boiled egg or so in each, covered in sauce.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot before adding the peeled eggs, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14 for the stew, then add the eggs evenly across containers. Each bowl comes out to about 574 calories with 54 grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: 3.5 lemons worth of lemon juice (164 g)
steps: Toss chunked chicken thighs with lemon juice and salt.
Slow-cook chopped red onions until deeply golden, then add garlic, ginger, and toasted berbere.
Stir in tomato paste and broth and simmer the sauce.
Braise the chicken to 165 F until the sauce thickens; finish with butter.
Add peeled hard boiled eggs and portion into 14 containers.
